significance.root_decision: The conjecture holds in all three cases and for every n: the two half twists (positive lifts of the longest elements on the intervals [1,a] and [b,n−1]) satisfy the braid relation of length N in the positive braid monoid, so they define a monoid homomorphism from the dihedral Artin monoid Br⁺(I₂(N)). Cases I and II follow from a periodic-braid identity: rotation and overlap identities for half twists, proved by positive rewriting. Case III (N = 6) comes from a seven-move identity on four strands, transported to all sizes by cabling with strands of unequal width. The source proves the subfamilies N = 3 (of case II) and N = 4, b ≥ 2 (of case I) and reports computer verification for n ≤ 15. Lean works in the presented positive monoid on σ₁, …, σ_{n−1} with the braid and commutation relations, defines the half twists as explicit triangular positive words, and proves both the alternating relation and the existence of the homomorphism with no premise beyond the conjecture's hypotheses; an earlier group-level proof is kept.
significance.caveat: Lean proves the relation and constructs the homomorphism for explicit triangular positive words. That those words are the source's positive lifts of the longest elements w₀ of the two parabolic subgroups is a written step: the words have the right number of letters in every rank and the right permutation (Lean checks the letter count in every rank and the reversal permutation at n = 4, 6, 7; the general statement is the standard inversion count in type A together with the Matsumoto–Tits theorem that all reduced words of an element give the same positive braid). The first version of the Lean packet proved the statement only in the braid group and assumed Garside's embedding for the monoid; the GPT-6.2 Sol cross-model review failed it for that, and stage 2 removed the assumption. MathDB 363298 is the same conjecture (from the authors' 2024 paper) and counts once with this one. The source proves two subfamilies (N = 3 and N = 4). No full prior resolution was found; V. Sury's 2026 thesis was screened by abstract only. Proof, first (same-model) review and Lean stage 1 are by Claude Opus 5.5; the cross-model review (mathematics correct, not routine 0.60), Lean stage 2 and the final check (a separate lane) are by GPT-6.2 Sol, so the final check is by the same model family as the stage-2 packager.

root_basis: Root (Claude Fable 5.2, 2026-11-23) extracted the 14 modules from the stage-2 appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, axioms_ok, no forbidden tokens; BGL.conj_6_35_monoid and BGL.conj_6_35_monoid_hom depend only on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound and take no hypothesis beyond BGL.Hyp n a b N), read the cross-model review and the final check, and ran the omega registry searches itself because the lanes' searches had been rate-limited. The cross-model review's one objection (the Garside premise) is removed by the stage-2 endpoints; the remaining written step (triangular word = positive lift of w₀) is named in the caveat and in the list of rows with a cited bridge.
